functions.name: readSkeletonData_deformTimelines

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_deformTimelines(Json* deform_map, void* data_raw, void* animation_raw, void* parser_raw)
abi.deform_map: the "deform" JSON child. Parent B3 caches it at [sp+0x50]; B14 loads it at 0x28e060, and at 0x28e0a0 REUSES the same slot for the malloc tag literal.
abi.data_raw: spSkeletonData* (parent [sp+0x18]); only the real findSkin / findSlotIndex / getAttachment walk it.
abi.animation_raw: spAnimation* (parent r11; 0x28e084 mov r10,r11 saves it, 0x28e334 mov r11,r10 restores it). The publish tail reads +0x04 duration, +0x08 timelineCount, +0x0c timelines.
abi.return: DEFORM_TL_REACHED_DRAWORDER 1 (0x28e068 / 0x28e07c / 0x28e334 fall-through to 0x28e338), DEFORM_TL_HANDOFF_ATTACHMENT 3 (0x28e110 beq 0x28e55c, E4 owns the rest).

functions.semantics: deform_map NULL -> drawOrder (0x28e060..0x28e068); skinNode = deform_map->child, NULL -> drawOrder (0x28e06c..0x28e07c). Four literals are materialised once (0x28e080..0x28e0b0): malloc tag -> [sp+0x50], "vertices" -> [sp+0x48], "offset" -> [sp+0x54], "time" -> [sp+0x58]. Skin loop (head 0x28e0b4, advance 0x28e320..0x28e330): skin = spSkeletonData_findSkin(data, skinNode->name) at 0x28e0c0 (result may be NULL and is NEVER tested; it is spilled to [sp+0x40]); slotNode = skinNode->child at 0x28e0c8. Slot loop (head 0x28e0dc, advance 0x28e310..0x28e31c): slotIndex = spSkeletonData_findSlotIndex(data, slotNode->name) at 0x28e0e4 (the -1 result is NOT tested); tlNode = slotNode->child at 0x28e0e8; both slotNode ([sp+0x5c]) and slotIndex ([sp+0x3c]) are spilled. Timeline loop (head 0x28e0fc, advance 0x28e2ec/0x28e30c): attachment = spSkin_getAttachment(skin, slotIndex, tlNode->name) at 0x28e108; NULL -> E4 handoff at 0x28e110. weighted = (attachment->bones != NULL) at 0x28e114..0x28e124; floatCount = weighted ? 2*(verticesCount/3) : verticesCount at 0x28e128..0x28e140; size = floatCount<<2 at 0x28e144; buffer = _malloc(size, tag, 388) at 0x28e14c..0x28e154; timeline = spDeformTimeline_create(tlNode->unk_0c, floatCount) at 0x28e158..0x28e164; timeline->slotIndex = slotIndex at 0x28e178; timeline->attachment = attachment at 0x28e17c; if tlNode->child != NULL the frame loop runs (0x28e180 beq skips it); _free(buffer) at 0x28e2c8; publish: timelineCount++ with timelines[count] = timeline (0x28e2cc..0x28e2e4), last = timeline->frames[declared-1] with a ONE-float stride (0x28e2e0..0x28e2f4), duration = max(duration,last) (0x28e2f8..0x28e308); tlNode = tlNode->next (0x28e2ec).

offset.role: spilled to [sp+0x54] at 0x28e0ac; Json_getInt at 0x28e1c0 with default 0

time.role: spilled to [sp+0x58] at 0x28e0b0; Json_getFloat at 0x28e284 with default 0.0f

malloc_tag.role: spilled to [sp+0x50] at 0x28e0a0 and handed to _malloc at 0x28e154

field_offsets.spSkeletonData.slotsCount: +0x18 (real findSlotIndex 0x28b0d4; this block only passes data through)
field_offsets.spVertexAttachment.bones: +0x14 (0x28e114 ldr r3,[r8,#0x14]; only tested for NULL — this is the weighted gate)
field_offsets.spVertexAttachment.vertices: +0x1c (0x28e24c base addend load; B14b 0x28e828 non-weighted frame source)
field_offsets.spDeformTimeline.frames: +0x10, ONE float per frame (0x282ecc store; 0x28e2e8 load; 0x28e2f0 lsl#2; 0x28e2f4 [r3,#-4])
field_offsets.spDeformTimeline.vertexFloatCount: +0x14 (0x282ed8 stores create's second arg; 0x282f3c/0x282f4c setFrame size/memcpy count)

malloc_388.line: 388 (0x28e150 mov r2,#388 — a plain MOV immediate, not movw, which is why the card extractor recorded null)
malloc_388.size_expression: (uint32_t)floatCount << 2 (0x28e144 lsl r2,r11,#2) where floatCount is r11 from the weighted split
malloc_388.ownership: freed once at 0x28e2c8 after the frame loop, on the path where no frames exist (0x28e180 beq 0x28e2c4) as well

create_abi.arguments: r0 = tlNode->unk_0c (declared frame count, 0x28e160); r1 = floatCount (0x28e158 mov r1,r11)
create_abi.body: calloc(1,36,tag,0x30f) 0x282e74..0x282e80; _spCurveTimeline_init(t,8,frameCount,...) 0x282e90..0x282ea4; +0x0c = frameCount 0x282eac; +0x10 = calloc(frameCount,4,tag,0x312) 0x282eb4..0x282ecc; +0x14 = r7 (SECOND argument) 0x282ed8; +0x18 = calloc(frameCount,4,tag,0x313) 0x282ed0..0x282edc

setframe_abi.arguments: r0 = timeline, r1 = frameIndex, r2 = time bits, r3 = vertices pointer
setframe_abi.body: 0x282f10 add r3,frames,i<<2 ; 0x282f18 str r2,[r3] -> frames[i] = time ; 0x282f14/0x282f1c free(old vertices[i]) ; 0x282f20 cmp r6,#0 -> 0x282f68 str NULL ; else 0x282f3c lsl r0,[r4,#0x14],#2 ; 0x282f40 _malloc(count*4,tag,799) ; 0x282f50 store ; 0x282f60 memcpy(count*4) — this is what pins +0x14 as the per-frame float-copy count

tail.frame_stride: ONE float: 0x28e2e0 ldr r2,[r9,#0xc] ; 0x28e2f0 add r3,r3,r2,lsl#2 ; 0x28e2f4 vldr s15,[r3,#-4] -> frames[declared-1]
tail.max_semantics: 0x28e2f8 vcmpe.f32 s14,s15 + 0x28e300 vmovgt.f32 s15,s14 -> duration is replaced only when strictly greater; an unordered (NaN) last frame keeps the old duration
tail.declared_vs_child: the frame loop follows the child list (0x28e2ac/0x28e2c0) while create and the duration index both use the declared count (0x28e160 and 0x28e2e0). declared=3 with one child reads frames[2], which create zero-filled
tail.publish_order: timelineCount is incremented (0x28e2d8) and timelines[count] stored (0x28e2e4) BEFORE the frames load (0x28e2e8) and the duration compare

quirks: The findSkin result is spilled to [sp+0x40] and never tested (0x28e0c0/0x28e0d4). A NULL skin is only observable later through getAttachment.

The findSlotIndex result is stored at [sp+0x3c] and fed to spSkin_getAttachment with NO -1 test (0x28e0e4/0x28e0f4). There is therefore no slot-not-found error on the deform path; E6 belongs to drawOrder (see the separate function entry).
B14 reuses [sp+0x50] for the malloc tag (0x28e0a0) after loading the deform node from it, so the tag literal replaces the map pointer in that slot.

The frame loop is skipped entirely when the attachment node has no child (0x28e180 beq 0x28e2c4), but the buffer is still allocated and freed and the timeline is still published with an all-zero frames array.
The weight/bone stream pointer at +0x14 is only compared against NULL; no element is dereferenced anywhere in B14/B14b.

functions.name: readSkeletonData_deformVertexFloatCount / readSkeletonData_deformWeightedDivide3

abi.return: the original r11: the per-frame vertex FLOAT count

functions.semantics: weighted = (attachment->bones != NULL) (0x28e114 ldr / 0x28e118 adds / 0x28e11c movne / 0x28e120 cmp / 0x28e124 str). weighted -> 0x28e128 ldrne r1,[sp,#0x60] (0x55555556), 0x28e12c ldrne r3,[r8,#0x18] (verticesCount), 0x28e134 smullne r1,r2,r1,r3, 0x28e13c subne r3,r2,r3,asr #31 (signed /3 truncating toward zero), 0x28e140 lslne r11,r3,#1 (x2). non-weighted -> 0x28e130 ldreq r11,[r8,#0x18] (verticesCount verbatim).

open_5_closure.question: census §7 open #5: the 2*(vertexCount/3) conversion and create's second argument were undefined
open_5_closure.answer: The branch condition is attachment+0x14 (the bone/weight stream pointer) being non-NULL. The conversion result r11 is the number of FLOATS the deform timeline stores per frame: it is create's second argument (0x28e158), the create body stores it at timeline+0x14 (0x282ed8), and setFrame uses +0x14 as the malloc size (0x282f3c lsl#2) and memcpy length (0x282f4c/0x282f60) of a fresh per-frame copy. The same r11 is the buffer's float count: malloc r11*4 (0x28e144), and the non-weighted base addend loop runs exactly r11 floats (0x28e244..0x28e270).

open_8_closure.question: census §7 open #8: the [sp+0x60] 0x55555556 constant — who else reads it and what is its signedness
open_8_closure.answer: Exactly one writer (B3: 0x28d2d8 movw r1,#0x5556 ; 0x28d2e0 movt r1,#0x5555 ; 0x28d304 str r1,[sp,#0x60]) and exactly one reader in the whole 13044-byte function (0x28e128 ldrne r1,[sp,#0x60]). B13 and B17 never touch it. The sequence smull + sub ... asr#31 is signed division by 3 truncating toward zero; the checker proves C's `/ 3` equals a bit-exact smull model over 25 values including INT_MIN and INT_MAX. INT_MIN -> 2*(-715827882) = -1431655764, and the lsl#2 byte size wraps to 0xAAAAAAB0.

functions.name: readSkeletonData_deformTimelineFrames

abi.signature: void readSkeletonData_deformTimelineFrames(Json* timelineNode, const void* attachment_raw, void* timeline_raw, float* buffer, int32_t floatCount, int32_t weighted, const void* parser_raw)
abi.timelineNode: the attachment-name JSON node (r9); its +0x04 child is the first frame and its +0x1c name is not used by the frames
abi.buffer: the r4 line-388 allocation, floatCount floats

functions.semantics: frame = timelineNode->child; NULL skips the loop on the caller side (0x28e180). Per frame: verticesJson = getItem(frame,"vertices") (0x28e1a4); offset = getInt(frame,"offset",0) (0x28e1c0); memset(buffer,0,offset*4) (0x28e1c8..0x28e1dc). If verticesJson is NULL (0x28e1ac beq -> B14b): weighted -> memset(buffer,0,floatCount*4) (0x28e830..0x28e840) and src = buffer; non-weighted -> src = attachment->vertices (+0x1c, 0x28e828) and the buffer is NOT initialised for this frame. Otherwise element = verticesJson->child (0x28e1f8); if parser->scale == 1.0f (0x28e1e8 vcmp / 0x28e1f4 vmrs / 0x28e1fc bne) each element's Json+0x18 float is copied verbatim (0x28e20c..0x28e21c); else each element is multiplied by parser->scale (B14b 0x28e858..0x28e874, vmul.f32) before the store; the copy starts at buffer + offset*4 (0x28e208) and the written counter starts at offset; then memset(buffer+written,0,(floatCount-written)*4) (0x28e224..0x28e238); src = buffer (0x28e274). Finally, if NOT weighted and floatCount > 0 (0x28e23c..0x28e250), buffer[i] += attachment->vertices[i] for ALL floatCount entries (0x28e258..0x28e270), then setFrame (0x28e298) and readCurve (0x28e2a8); frame = frame->next and frameIndex++ (0x28e2ac..0x28e2bc); loop while frame != NULL (0x28e2c0).
quirks: The scaled copy's first iteration reuses the s15 value loaded at 0x28e1e4 (parser->scale); later iterations reload it at 0x28e858. The arithmetic result is the same.

The non-weighted base addend runs over the WHOLE floatCount-float buffer, including the zero-filled prefix and tail, not just the copied elements. frame_base_add pins this with base 10/20/30/40 and deltas 1/2 -> 10,20,31,42.
When the vertices key is absent and the attachment is non-weighted, the buffer is left at its previous contents but is not the published pointer; setFrame receives attachment+0x1c instead.

There is no bounds check between the JSON array length and floatCount: a longer array writes past the buffer and makes (floatCount-written) negative, i.e. a huge tail memset. The fixture never drives that shape; the mutants are designed so this unbounded path is not hit before a named assertion fires.

open: The weighted vertex stream's real element layout (why 3 floats per deformed vertex collapse to 2) is not recovered: only the division by 3 and the x2 are proven. Any statement about bone indices or weights would need the spVertexAttachment consumer (apply/render), outside this block.
E4 (0x28e55c, "Attachment not found: ") is left to its own module; this driver only reports the handoff.
The deform timeline's apply path (spDeformTimeline_apply) is not recovered, so the run-time consequence of +0x1c slotIndex / +0x20 attachment / +0x14 copy count is stated from the write side only.
declared frame count == 0 reaches the tail and indexes frames[-1] in 32-bit wrap arithmetic; the fixture never drives that (same restriction as the other timeline modules).

A frame whose "vertices" array is longer than floatCount - offset overruns the buffer and makes the tail memset length negative; the original has no check. The fixture avoids that shape, and the mutation set is ordered so no mutant reaches it before a named assertion.
spDeformTimeline_create/setFrame bodies are read statically but not translated; their line numbers (0x30f/0x312/0x313/799) are recorded from the disassembly, not asserted at run time.
